sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《你二十多岁的心理学》，这是一档探讨我们二十多岁时所经历的重大人生变化

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 和转折，以及它们对我们心理意味着什么的播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, I am so glad to have you here for an episode, for a topic I'm really, really passionate about.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何方，我都很高兴你能来收听这一期节目，探讨一个我非常、非常热衷的话题。

sentences.en: It is possibly one of my strongest opinions.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我最坚定的观点之一。

sentences.en: I don't even think it's a controversial one.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这甚至算不上什么争议性话题。

sentences.en: I want to talk about why I believe so deeply that one of the best things we can do in our 20s is fall in love with our own company.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈为什么我深信，我们在二十多岁时能做的最好的事情之一，就是学会享受独处。

sentences.en: And I want to talk about why that is, but more specifically, how we can do that, especially in a world where we are more addicted to social contact and engagement,
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈为什么会这样，更具体地说，我们该如何做到这一点，尤其是在这样一个我们比以往任何时候都更沉迷于社交接触、互动

sentences.en: stimulation than ever before.
sentences.zh: 和刺激的世界里。

sentences.en: When I think actually having a moment of true solitude is increasingly rare.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为拥有真正独处的时刻正变得越来越稀缺。

sentences.en: It's still very much possible.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然是非常可能的。

sentences.en: And I think it's a necessity if you want to deepen the relationship that you have with yourself and as a result, the people around you.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果你想加深与自己的关系，并进而改善与周围人的关系，这是一种必然。

sentences.en: Honestly, I think every aspect of your life becomes more defined and sharper and intentional when we value our own free time and our own company.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为当我们重视自己的空闲时间和独处时，生活的方方面面都会变得更加清晰、明确和有目的性。

sentences.en: And we see that space and that time being alone with ourselves as a source of peace, as a source of contemplation and growth, rather than just as empty space
sentences.zh: 我们将那种与自己独处的空间和时间视为平静、沉思和成长的源泉，而不是仅仅将其视为需要用社交应酬、工作或任何类似事物来填补的

sentences.en: that we need to fill with social commitments, with work, with anything of the sort.
sentences.zh: 空白时间。

sentences.en: I think it comes back to that very core foundational philosophy we have on the show, that the relationship you have with yourself is your biggest and most important investment.
sentences.zh: 我认为这归根结底是我们节目中那个最核心的基础哲学：你与自己的关系是你最大、最重要的投资。

sentences.en: And when you neglect it, I think everything else in your life tends to suffer as well.
sentences.zh: 当你忽视它时，我认为你生活中的一切往往也会随之受损。

sentences.en: No one can sustain you, can know you like you know yourself.
sentences.zh: 没有人能像你了解自己那样去支撑你、了解你。

sentences.en: And so you have to make that relationship a priority, even when it's not easy, even when it's not convenient, even when it doesn't come naturally to you.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须把这种关系放在首位，即使在不容易、不方便，或者感觉不自然的时候也是如此。

sentences.en: So I have always had, I think a really complicated relationship with loneliness just to get vulnerable for a second.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想先坦诚一点，我一直以来与孤独的关系其实非常复杂。

sentences.en: And I think it really stems quite honestly from being bullied as a child.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为这确实源于我小时候被霸凌的经历。

sentences.en: I was a really strange kid.
sentences.zh: 我小时候是个很奇怪的孩子。

sentences.en: I didn't have many friends.
sentences.zh: 我没什么朋友。

sentences.en: I was always kind of made to play like the villain character when we were playing make-believe.
sentences.zh: 玩过家家的时候，我总是被安排扮演反派角色。

sentences.en: I was a bit shy.
sentences.zh: 我有点害羞。

sentences.en: I was just a bit different, which is something that I love now because I think weird kids turn into interesting adults.
sentences.zh: 我只是有点与众不同，而这正是我现在所热爱的一点，因为我认为奇怪的孩子长大后会变成有趣的大人。

sentences.en: But because there was this whole period in my younger years, in my formative years, where I never quite felt like I belonged, I knew what it felt like
sentences.zh: 但因为在我年轻时、在我成长的岁月里，有那么长一段时间我从未真正感到归属感，所以我很小的时候就知道

sentences.en: to be quite lonely from a young age.
sentences.zh: 孤独是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And I did get really comfortable with my own company.
sentences.zh: 我也确实变得非常习惯于独处。

sentences.en: It was like kind of a bit of a superpower for myself.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说就像是一种超能力。

sentences.en: As sad as it sounds, right?
sentences.zh: 听起来很可悲，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, you know, I get that it's very kind of sad.
sentences.zh: 我知道，这听起来确实挺可悲的。

sentences.en: Like you didn't have enough friends, so you had to be your own best friend.
sentences.zh: 就像是说，你没有足够的朋友，所以你不得不成为自己最好的朋友。

sentences.en: And I really actually valued that about myself.
sentences.zh: 而我实际上非常珍视自己的这一点。

sentences.en: But when I got to uni,
sentences.zh: 但当我上了大学，

sentences.en: I've spoken about this before, but I really met my people.
sentences.zh: 我之前提到过，我真的遇到了属于我的圈子。

sentences.en: I got to meet the people I still call my best friends, even now.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了那些直到现在我仍称之为挚友的人。

sentences.en: And of course, it was like the best thing ever.
sentences.zh: 当然，那感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: This is what I always wanted.
sentences.zh: 这正是我一直想要的。

sentences.en: But because this was such a new experience to constantly have people I wanted to be around who made my life so much better, who were really tired to me at the hip for a long time,
sentences.zh: 但因为这种体验太新奇了，我身边总是围绕着我想在一起的人，他们让我的生活变得如此美好，而且很长一段时间里我们都形影不离，

sentences.en: I kind of forgot how to be alone.
sentences.zh: 我反而有点忘记了该如何独处。

sentences.en: You know, that survival skill, that protective mechanism I developed of valuing my own company was no longer useful in this situation, so I neglected it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种我曾经培养出来的生存技能，那种珍视独处的保护机制，在这种情况下不再有用了，所以我忽视了它。

sentences.en: And eventually, it was something that I had to relearn, especially as I transitioned kind of out of my early 20s when I was at uni and I was surrounded by people all the time
sentences.zh: 最终，我不得不重新学习，尤其是在我从大学时代二十出头、身边总是围满人的状态，过渡到我现在这种全职工作、搬到一个朋友不多的新城市的生活时，

sentences.en: to the situation I'm in now, where I was working full time, I moved to a new city where I didn't have as many friends.
sentences.zh: 我突然又单身了。

sentences.en: I was suddenly single as well.
sentences.zh: 这感觉和我小时候的感觉太像了。

sentences.en: It felt so similar to how I had felt as a child.
sentences.zh: 但我已经失去了我的应对技能。

sentences.en: But I had lost my coping skill.
sentences.zh: 我失去了，

sentences.en: I had lost,
sentences.zh: 我想，那种我在独处中感受到的敬畏和快乐。

sentences.en: I think, the reverence and the joy I felt in my own company.
sentences.zh: 我开始意识到，这段过渡期之所以如此艰难，是因为在那之前的最后三四年里，

sentences.en: And I really kind of began to notice that the reason this was so difficult, this transitionary period, was because for the last three or four years before that time,
sentences.zh: 我并没有在与自己的关系上投入任何精力。

sentences.en: I hadn't really put any effort into the relationship I had with myself.
sentences.zh: 我总是优先考虑与他人的时间和经历，最终这反而损害了我自己。

sentences.en: I was always prioritizing time and experiences with others and it eventually came at my detriment.
sentences.zh: 我认为作为一个世代，包括我们在内，我们很难花时间独处，原因有几个。

sentences.en: I think as a generation, all of us included, we have a hard time spending time alone for a few reasons.
sentences.zh: 最大的因素是 FOMO，即臭名昭著的“错失恐惧症”。

sentences.en: The biggest contributor is FOMO, the infamous fear of missing out.
sentences.zh: 而这种错失恐惧症包含两个方面。

sentences.en: And the fear of missing out is twofold.
sentences.zh: 首先，它涉及一种感知，随后是一种强迫行为。

sentences.en: Firstly, it involves a perception followed by a compulsion.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们确实倾向于夸大我们认为别人在没有我们参与的情况下所获得的快乐和质量。

sentences.en: So, we really tend to exaggerate the quality and the fun we think everybody else is having without us.
sentences.zh: 因此，在那些我们不在场的时刻，我们真的倾向于放大我们认为别人正在经历的事情，并倾向于让它看起来比实际情况要宏大、金光闪闪

sentences.en: So, in those moments when we're not present, we really tend to, like, expand what we think other people are experiencing and we tend to make it seem a lot bigger and more golden
sentences.zh: 且丰富多彩得多。

sentences.en: and colourful than it actually is.
sentences.zh: 这导致我们从不想错过任何活动，从不想没有计划或被排除在外，这是一种强迫行为，对吧？

sentences.en: And this results in us never wanting to miss an event, never wanting to be without plans or excluded, which is a compulsion, right?
sentences.zh: 我们似乎被迫不断地参与其中，不断地卷入其中，这几乎是为了缓解那种我们正在错失什么的恐惧。

sentences.en: We are kind of compelled to constantly be engaged and constantly be involved almost as a way to soothe that fear that we're missing out.
sentences.zh: 现在需要指出的是，这个词，

sentences.en: Now, it should be noted that this term,
sentences.zh: FOMO，最早是在 2004 年提出的。

sentences.en: FOMO, was first introduced in 2004.
sentences.zh: 那正是 Facebook 成立的同一年。

sentences.en: That is the same year that Facebook launched.
sentences.zh: 它在 2010 年代初开始真正流行起来，这是社交媒体日益普及的直接后果，它为人们提供了不断观察他人动态的机会，

sentences.en: And it began to really take off in the early 2010s as a direct consequence of this increasing uptake of social media and the opportunities it provided for people to constantly
sentences.zh: 并将此与他们自己的日子和生活进行比较。

sentences.en: see what others were up to and to compare that to their own days and their own lives.
sentences.zh: 现在，在当今社会，我们比以往任何时候都更容易接触到关于他人正在做什么的如此多的细节，甚至是私密的细节。

sentences.en: Now, more than ever, at this point in society, we are exposed to so many details, intimate details, about what others are doing.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们面临着持续的不确定性：我们做得够不够？我们是否获得了足够的社交联系？我们认识的人是否

sentences.en: And that means that we're faced with this continuous uncertainty about whether we're doing enough, whether we are getting enough social connection, whether we know as many people
sentences.zh: 足够多？我们的友谊是否像我们希望的那样成功？

sentences.en: as we should, whether our friendships are as successful as we would want them to be.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这让社交变得相当具有竞争性。

sentences.en: So I think it kind of makes socializing quite competitive.
sentences.zh: 如果我们的目标总是像别人一样忙碌，从不让那些 FOMO 的负面情绪进入我们的生活，那么我们确实剥夺了自己去珍惜独处时光的机会

sentences.en: And if our aim is to always be as busy as the next person and never let those negative feelings of FOMO into our lives, then we do really deprive ourselves of the opportunity
sentences.zh: 和那种美好。

sentences.en: and the beauty of cherishing our alone time.
sentences.zh: 研究人员还认为，

sentences.en: Researchers also believe that
sentences.zh: FOMO 使我们对社交排斥的感觉特别敏感，无论这种社交排斥是感知的还是真实的。

sentences.en: FOMO makes us particularly attuned to feelings of social rejection, whether that social rejection is perceived or real.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，在心理和情感层面上，被拒绝的痛苦确实模仿了我们在面对身体

sentences.en: And we know that on a psychological and emotional level that the pain of rejection really mimics the same kind of discomfort we feel in response to physically
sentences.zh: 疼痛刺激和伤害时所感受到的那种不适。

sentences.en: painful stimuli and injury.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想要避免它。

sentences.en: So we want to avoid it.
sentences.zh: 但错过一些计划并不会毁了你的生活。

sentences.en: But missing out on plans won't ruin your life.
sentences.zh: 它不会像手臂骨折或腿部骨折那样让你动弹不得。

sentences.en: It won't immobilize you the same way that a broken arm or a fractured leg will.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个因为周六晚上没有计划，

sentences.en: If you are someone who freaks out at not having plans on a
sentences.zh: 或者哪怕只是独自度过一个晚上就会抓狂的人，

sentences.en: Saturday night or spending even a single evening alone,
sentences.zh: 我认为你真的需要考虑一下，这到底是真正的孤独，你是否真的需要更多的社交联系，还是说这只是 FOMO，你只需要

sentences.en: I think it's really time to consider whether this is actually genuine loneliness, whether you actually need more social connection, or whether it's FOMO and you just need to
sentences.zh: 重新构建你与自己独处的关系。

sentences.en: reframe your relationship with your own company.
sentences.zh: 我认为这还归结于这样一个事实：作为一个社会，我们对孤独并没有建立起健康的关系。

sentences.en: I think it also comes down to the fact that as a society we just don't have a healthy relationship with loneliness.
sentences.zh: 我们将其视为需要避免的东西，我们给它贴上污名，我们害怕它，而不是在我们的生活中为它留出空间，去认识到它首先能教给我们什么，它有多么普遍，

sentences.en: We see it as something to avoid, we stigmatize it, we fear it, rather than actually holding space for it in our lives and recognizing what it firstly has to teach us, how universal
sentences.zh: 以及第三，它实际上如何能帮助我们培养一个更丰富、我认为更深邃的内心世界。

sentences.en: it is, and thirdly how it can actually help us cultivate a richer and I would say deeper inner world.
sentences.zh: 孤独，让我们搞清楚，它只是你身体发出的一个信号。

sentences.en: Loneliness, let's get this straight, it is just a cue from your body.
sentences.zh: 就像饥饿是在告诉你该补充能量、该吃饭了，口渴是在告诉你该喝水了，疲劳和困倦是在告诉你该

sentences.en: The same way that hunger is telling you it's time to fuel, it's time to eat, thirst is telling you it's time to drink, fatigue, tiredness are telling you it's time to
sentences.zh: 休息了，孤独是在告诉你该去建立联系了，或者该静下心来与自己相处，弄清楚为什么你会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: rest, loneliness is telling you that it's time to connect, or it's time to sit with yourself and figure out why it is that you feel that way.
sentences.zh: 同样重要的是要注意，我们过度社交的次数越多，我们对令人满意的社交联系的阈值就越高，我们需要的就越多。

sentences.en: It's also important to note that the more we excessively socialize, the higher our threshold for satisfying social connection becomes, the more we need.
sentences.zh: 试着这样想，对吧，在高中时你很可能每天都能见到朋友，分开一天都会觉得很奇怪。

sentences.en: Kind of think about it this way, right, at high school you saw your friends every single day, most likely, and one day apart felt really strange.
sentences.zh: 当我们进入二十多岁，

sentences.en: When we get into our
sentences.zh: 尤其是二十多岁后期，

sentences.en: 20s, especially our later
sentences.zh: 我们见到其他人的水平和能力自然会下降一些，但如果你已经变得，如果你发现独处变得非常困难，如果你太

sentences.en: 20s, our level and our capacity for seeing other people naturally goes down a bit, but if you have become, if it's become very difficult for you to spend time alone, if you're so
sentences.zh: 习惯于身边总是有人，那么你维持那种填满日程表、总是和人在一起、从不给自己留片刻时间的冲动越久，

sentences.en: used to having people around you constantly, the more that you sustain the urge to book out your calendars, to always be around people, to never have a moment for yourself, the
sentences.zh: 你就越无法忍受那些你不得不享受独处的时光。

sentences.en: less you are able to tolerate the times when you do have to enjoy your own company.
sentences.zh: 生活中会有一些你感到孤独的时期，但如果你从未给自己机会去感受那种状态，去适应那种情况，去拥抱一段时间的“独行侠”生活，哪怕是快乐的独行侠，当你最终发现自己处于那个时期、那个篇章、那个孤独的季节时，它会变得更加
